blocks.content: To detect the duplicate characters in the string, we will count the number of times each character appears in the string. If a character appears more than once, we will consider it as a duplicate character.
We will use HashMap to find duplicate characters in a string as it allows us to store each character as a key and its corresponding count as value.
To find the repeated character in giggle string in the HashMap, we will loop through each character in the string and check whether it exists in the HashMap.
If it does, we will increase its value by 1. Otherwise, we will add it to the HashMap with a value of 1.
Here, we have the frequency of character in the "giggle" string. Now, if the count of the character it is more than 1, it is the repeated character.
Now, let's see how we can implement this logic in our program.

items: Create an empty HashMap to store the characters and their counts. The keys will be of Character type and the values will be of Integer type.
Use a for loop to iterate through the input String, one character at a time.
Get the current character in the loop using the charAt method and store it in a variable of Character type.

Check if the current character is already in the HashMap using the containsKey() method. If the character is in the map, increment its count by 1 by using the put method to update the existing key-value pair in the HashMap.
If the character is not already in the HashMap, add the character to the map with a count of 1 using the put() method.
After the for loop, create an empty ArrayList to store the repeated characters.
Use a for-each loop to iterate through each key-value pair in the HashMap using the entrySet() method.
Check whether the value of the current key (i.e. the count of the current character) is greater than 1 using an if statement.
If the count is greater than 1, add the key (i.e. the repeated character) to the ArrayList using the add method.
After the for-each loop, return the ArrayList containing the repeated characters.
